paper.title: UniTracker: Learning Universal Whole-Body Motion Tracker for Humanoid Robots

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It source-locks a reference-conditioned whole-body tracker's corpus admission, retargeting, frame transforms, reference horizons, privileged-teacher boundary, fixed tracking objective, and independent metrics. These details constrain the manifest that Sam must freeze while changing only reference/oracle logic or a separate task reward.
not_evidence_for: An OGMP state machine, predicate transition, or composition of multiple reference clips
Improvement of a task reward under a fixed tracking objective
A causal benefit from dataset filtering or retargeting alone
Universal generalization on an aggregate held-out motion benchmark
Any implemented UniTracker capability in RL-Sculptor

mechanisms.name: Curated and retargeted motion reference corpus
mechanisms.description: AMASS clips with object interactions or fewer than ten frames are removed, PHC filtering rejects unsuitable motions, and sixteen body-link correspondences drive sequence-level SMPL-to-G1 retargeting.

mechanisms.name: Privileged next-frame teacher
mechanisms.description: A PPO teacher observes full simulator state and local-frame one-step differences to the reference, producing high-fidelity action supervision for online distillation.

mechanisms.name: Reference-conditioned CVAE online distillation
mechanisms.description: A full-observation encoder is KL-aligned to a deployable prior conditioned on partial proprioception and five future reference steps; a decoder maps deployable history and latent state to actions under teacher supervision.

mechanisms.name: Frozen-base residual fast adaptation
mechanisms.description: For references the universal policy cannot track, all base parameters are frozen and an RL-trained decoder adds a task-specific correction to the base action.

mechanisms.name: Whole-body tracking objective bundle
mechanisms.description: Seven reference-tracking terms are combined with action-rate, torque, slippage, and termination terms; regularization and penalty terms are introduced by an unspecified curriculum.

parameters.name: curated_training_motion_count
parameters.context: AMASS-derived corpus after object-interaction, short-clip, and PHC filtering.

parameters.name: excluded_short_clip_threshold
parameters.context: Clips shorter than this threshold are discarded.

parameters.name: retargeting_correspondence_count
parameters.context: Corresponding SMPL and humanoid links selected for retargeting.

parameters.name: robot_total_dof
parameters.context: Unitree G1 embodiment used in simulation and hardware evaluation.

parameters.name: controlled_action_dimension
parameters.context: Six wrist joints are locked; actions are executed through a PD controller.

parameters.name: projected_gravity_termination_threshold
parameters.context: Episode terminates if projected gravity on the x or y axis exceeds this value.

parameters.name: mean_link_tracking_termination_threshold
parameters.context: Episode terminates when mean robot-reference link distance exceeds this value.

parameters.name: deploy_proprioceptive_history
parameters.context: Authors describe joint states, root angular velocity, gravity, and previous actions as stacked over the past 25 steps.

parameters.name: deploy_future_reference_window
parameters.context: Future goal features are stacked over five steps; frame transforms differ between root features and body positions.

parameters.name: tracking_objective_weights
parameters.context: Weights printed in Table I; this is the fixed foundation tracking objective for Sam's boundary, not the separate task-reward knob.

parameters.name: selected_cvae_latent_dimension
parameters.context: Selected from 32, 64, 128, and 256 in the architecture ablation.

parameters.name: simulation_parallel_environment_count
parameters.context: Isaac Gym training under domain randomization.

parameters.name: all_amass_train_success_rate
parameters.context: Ours row on the full AMASS training dataset; DAgger without CVAE is 88.03 +/- 0.221.

parameters.name: all_amass_train_mpkpe
parameters.context: Ours row on the full AMASS training dataset; Table II does not state a unit.

parameters.name: noise_level_2_success_rate
parameters.context: UniTracker at ordinal noise level 2; DAgger without CVAE is 79.58 +/- 0.066. The perturbation magnitude is not defined.

failure_modes.name: Rare and dynamic reference failure
failure_modes.description: The universal policy is not expected to track every rare, strongly out-of-distribution, or near-physical-limit sequence; the proposed remedy changes the policy through residual adaptation.

failure_modes.name: Explicit-reference latent bypass
failure_modes.description: When the actor receives the reference directly, the latent variable's influence vanishes and behavior resembles standard DAgger.

failure_modes.name: Large latent training difficulty
failure_modes.description: Latent dimensions above 64 were reported as harder to train and did not improve overall performance.

failure_modes.name: Train-set headline and limited held-out aggregate
failure_modes.description: The main aggregate table is explicitly evaluated on the AMASS training dataset; held-out support is an illustrated unseen crescent kick and supplemental demonstrations rather than an aggregate held-out corpus result.

failure_modes.name: Under-specified training and perturbation details
failure_modes.description: Version 3 does not give PPO hyperparameters, domain-randomization ranges, reward-curriculum schedule, numerical noise magnitudes, or a numeric adaptation-time comparison.

failure_modes.name: Qualitative hardware evidence
failure_modes.description: The paper and project page show real G1 behaviors but report no aggregate hardware success rate, trial count, or confidence interval.

evaluation.name: AMASS training-corpus comparison and ablation
evaluation.description: UniTracker is compared with OmniH2O, ExBody2, DAgger without CVAE, and scratch training; architecture, KL residual/coefficient, future-window, and latent-size variants are tested.

evaluation.name: Independent motion-tracking metric set
evaluation.description: Evaluation separates success rate, world-frame mean per-keypoint position error, joint-velocity distance, and joint-acceleration distance.

evaluation.name: Ordinal observation-noise robustness
evaluation.description: UniTracker and DAgger without CVAE are compared at noise levels 0, 1, and 2; UniTracker degrades more slowly, but the physical scales are not defined.

evaluation.name: Qualitative OOD and global-consistency examples
evaluation.description: A MuJoCo crescent kick unseen during training and a walking trajectory compare CVAE and non-CVAE behavior; project videos add real-world OOD demonstrations.

evaluation.name: Fast-adaptation convergence figure
evaluation.description: Residual adaptation is compared with scratch training on one challenging sequence and the AMASS test dataset using episode length and cumulative reward, without tabulated convergence times.

evaluation.name: Unitree G1 real-world demonstrations
evaluation.description: The project demonstrates universal-policy motions, fast-adapted motions, text-to-motion, and video-estimated references on G1 without aggregate reliability statistics.

evidence.claim: The framework has a privileged PPO teacher, CVAE-based online distillation, and residual fast-adaptation stages.

evidence.locator: Section II-B, Humanoid Motion Dataset Curation
evidence.claim: Object-interaction clips and clips shorter than ten frames are removed, PHC filtering leaves 8,179 motions, and sixteen link correspondences drive two-stage retargeting.

evidence.locator: Section II-C, Oracle Policy Training in Simulation
evidence.claim: The teacher observes full simulator state and next-frame local reference differences; early termination thresholds are projected gravity 0.8 and mean link distance 0.5 m; only asset properties are randomized in Stage 1.

evidence.locator: Table I, Definition of Reward Functions; Section II-C, Reward Design
evidence.claim: The training objective combines seven tracking terms with action-rate, torque, slippage, and termination terms; the paper says regularization and penalties follow a curriculum without giving its schedule.

evidence.locator: Section II-D, Hierarchical Controller via Online Distillation; Equations 1-3
evidence.claim: Deployable input uses 25-step proprioceptive history and five future reference steps; the CVAE aligns a full-state encoder with a partial-state conditional prior and learns from teacher action supervision.

evidence.locator: Section II-E, Fast Adaption on top of a Universal Policy; Equation 4
evidence.claim: Rare, OOD, and highly dynamic failed references are handled by freezing the universal policy and RL-training an explicit-reference residual decoder whose output is added to the base action.

evidence.locator: Table II, Baselines Comparison and Ablation Studies
evidence.claim: On the AMASS training dataset, UniTracker reports 91.82 +/- 0.114 success and 82.57 +/- 0.097 MPKPE; the table tests direct reference input, KL residual/coefficient, future window, and latent dimension.
Training uses 8,192 Isaac Gym environments; evaluation defines SR, world-frame MPKPE, velocity distance, and acceleration distance; hardware is a 29-DoF G1 with 23 controlled DoFs.

Direct actor reference input suppresses the latent; dimension 64, future window five, and KL coefficient 0.1 are selected; an unseen crescent kick and straight-walking trajectory provide qualitative generalization/global-consistency evidence.
At ordinal noise level 2, UniTracker reports 86.78 +/- 0.212 success versus 79.58 +/- 0.066 without CVAE; the table does not define numerical perturbation magnitudes.

evidence.locator: Section III-E, Light Weight Fast Adaption; Figure 5
evidence.claim: Fast adaptation is compared with scratch training on one challenging sequence and the AMASS test dataset using episode length and cumulative reward, but no tabular convergence time is supplied.

evidence.locator: Official project page: behavior, fast-adaptation, and downstream-application sections
evidence.claim: The authors provide videos for universal-policy behaviors, fast-adapted motions, text-to-motion references, and video-estimated references; the page gives no aggregate hardware success statistic.
